What causes people to behave as they do?

According to the�behaviourists, great deals of a youngster s actions are shaped by the behavior of those around him. The child often imitates the actions of others. They youngster will then decide whether these actions will become a permanent part of his or her approach to life depending on whether the behavior is rewarded or punished.

This means that a person is programmed by environmental forces. If a reward is offered repeatedly for a behavior, the individual will retain that response. If punishment follows a behavior, the person will quickly abandon that action.

For example, Behaviourist principles are often used when training an animal. When the pet displays good behavior, she is rewarded; when she misbehaves, she is punished.�

The rewards and punishments people give to each other are not always obvious, like money and gifts or slaps and scoldings. Subtle yet powerful rewards are smiles or nods; frowns and silence are subtle forms of punishment.
